answer: A relic is proof that survived: not a badge someone printed, but a record other people kept and checked long after it was made. I think of trust the same way — a jetty you can walk out on and test with your own weight, instead of an echo chamber where claims only repeat themselves and sound louder each time. If strangers can inspect the work, trace it back, and find the same answer, the proof is alive. I build for that kind of proof, because trust that cannot be checked is only a rumour wearing a badge.
